name: Easy Run
instructions: Start at a comfortable, conversational pace.
Maintain relaxed shoulders and a slight forward lean.
Keep your breathing steady and controlled throughout.
Run for the prescribed duration, typically 30-60 minutes.
You should be able to hold a conversation at this effort level.

name: Long Run
instructions: Begin at an easy, sustainable pace.
Focus on maintaining consistent effort rather than speed.
Hydrate at regular intervals, roughly every 20-30 minutes.
Gradually increase distance week over week by no more than 10%.
Run for 60-150 minutes depending on training plan.

name: Tempo Run
instructions: Warm up with 10-15 minutes of easy running.
Increase pace to a comfortably hard effort, roughly 80-85% max heart rate.
Maintain this pace for 20-40 minutes.
You should be able to speak in short phrases but not full sentences.
Cool down with 10 minutes of easy jogging.

name: Progression Run
instructions: Start at an easy, relaxed pace for the first third of your run.
Gradually increase pace to a moderate effort for the middle third.
Finish the final third at tempo or threshold pace.
Each segment should feel noticeably faster than the previous one.
Total run duration is typically 40-60 minutes.

name: Fartlek Run
instructions: Warm up with 10 minutes of easy jogging.
Alternate between faster surges and easy recovery jogs.
Vary the length and intensity of surges based on feel.
Use landmarks like trees or lampposts to mark surge intervals.
Continue for 20-40 minutes, then cool down with easy jogging.

name: Negative Split Run
instructions: Plan to run the second half faster than the first half.
Start conservatively at an easy to moderate pace.
At the halfway point, begin gradually increasing your effort.
Finish the final miles at a strong, controlled pace.
This teaches patience and race-day pacing strategy.

name: Steady State Run
instructions: Warm up with 10 minutes of easy jogging.
Settle into a pace that is moderately hard, slightly easier than tempo.
Hold this effort consistently for 25-45 minutes.
Focus on even breathing and relaxed form throughout.
Cool down with 10 minutes of easy jogging.

name: Recovery Run
instructions: Run at a very easy, relaxed pace.
Keep heart rate in zone 1-2, well below conversational effort.
Duration is typically 20-40 minutes.
Focus on loose, relaxed form with short strides.
This run promotes blood flow and aids recovery from hard sessions.

name: 400m Intervals
instructions: Warm up with 15 minutes of easy jogging and dynamic drills.
Run 400 meters at a hard effort, roughly 90-95% max effort.
Recover with 200-400 meters of easy jogging between intervals.
Repeat for 6-12 repetitions depending on fitness level.
Cool down with 10 minutes of easy jogging.

name: 800m Intervals
instructions: Warm up with 15 minutes of easy jogging and strides.
Run 800 meters at a hard, controlled effort.
Recover with 400 meters of easy jogging between repeats.
Complete 4-8 repetitions.
Cool down with 10 minutes of easy jogging and stretching.

name: Mile Repeats
instructions: Warm up with 15 minutes of easy running and dynamic drills.
Run 1 mile at threshold to 5K race pace.
Recover with 3-4 minutes of easy jogging between repeats.
Complete 3-6 repetitions based on fitness and goal race.
Cool down with 10-15 minutes of easy jogging.

name: Sprint Intervals
instructions: Warm up thoroughly with 10 minutes of jogging and dynamic stretches.
Sprint at 95-100% effort for 100-200 meters.
Walk or jog slowly for 60-90 seconds to recover.
Repeat for 8-12 sprints.
Cool down with 10 minutes of walking and stretching.

name: Hill Sprints
instructions: Find a hill with a moderate 4-8% grade.
Warm up with 10-15 minutes of easy jogging on flat ground.
Sprint uphill for 8-15 seconds at maximum effort.
Walk back down for full recovery between sprints.
Start with 4-6 repeats and build up to 10-12 over weeks.

name: Strides
instructions: After an easy run, find a flat stretch of 80-100 meters.
Gradually accelerate to about 90% of max speed over the first 30 meters.
Hold that pace through the middle, then decelerate smoothly.
Walk back to the start for full recovery.
Complete 4-6 strides, focusing on smooth, relaxed form.

name: Ladder Intervals
instructions: Warm up with 15 minutes of easy running.
Run 200m, 400m, 800m, 1200m, 800m, 400m, 200m at progressively harder efforts.
Take equal-distance recovery jogs between each interval.
The longest interval should be at roughly tempo effort.
Cool down with 10 minutes of easy jogging.

name: Tabata Sprints
instructions: Warm up with 10-15 minutes of easy jogging and dynamic stretches.
Sprint at maximum effort for 20 seconds.
Rest or walk for 10 seconds.
Repeat for 8 rounds totaling 4 minutes.
Cool down with 10 minutes of walking and stretching.

name: 200m Repeats
instructions: Warm up with 15 minutes of jogging, drills, and strides.
Run 200 meters at 95% effort.
Recover with 200 meters of walking or easy jogging.
Complete 8-16 repetitions.
Cool down with 10 minutes of easy jogging.

name: A-Skip
instructions: Stand tall with good posture.
Skip forward, driving one knee up to hip height on each skip.
Keep the support leg straight and push off the ball of the foot.
Maintain an upright torso and pump your arms in sync.
Cover 30-50 meters per set, repeat 2-3 times.

name: B-Skip
instructions: Begin like an A-Skip by driving the knee up to hip height.
At the top of the knee drive, extend the leg forward.
Actively pull the foot back down and underneath your body.
This pawing motion reinforces proper ground contact mechanics.
Cover 30-50 meters per set, repeat 2-3 times.

name: High Knees
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Drive one knee up to hip height while pushing off the opposite foot.
Alternate legs rapidly in a running motion.
Stay on the balls of your feet and pump your arms.
Perform for 20-30 seconds or 30-50 meters.

name: Butt Kicks
instructions: Stand tall and begin jogging in place or moving forward.
Focus on kicking your heels up toward your glutes.
Keep your thighs relatively vertical; the motion is in the lower leg.
Maintain a quick cadence and light foot contacts.
Perform for 20-30 seconds or 30-50 meters.

name: Carioca (Grapevine)
instructions: Stand sideways to the direction of travel.
Cross your trailing foot in front, then step sideways with the lead foot.
Cross the trailing foot behind, then step sideways again.
Rotate your hips with each crossover while keeping shoulders square.
Cover 30-50 meters, then repeat facing the opposite direction.

name: Bounding
instructions: Begin with a few jogging steps to build momentum.
Push off powerfully from one foot, driving the opposite knee high.
Aim for maximum distance and hang time on each bound.
Land softly on the opposite foot and immediately push off again.
Cover 30-50 meters per set, repeat 2-4 times.

name: Ankle Hops
instructions: Stand tall with feet together.
Hop forward using only your ankles; keep knees nearly straight.
Focus on quick, springy contacts with the ground.
Minimize ground contact time and use your calf muscles to propel.
Cover 20-30 meters per set, repeat 2-3 times.

name: Single-Leg Hops
instructions: Stand on one foot with good balance.
Hop forward on that single leg, driving off the ball of your foot.
Use your arms for momentum and balance.
Land softly and spring forward on each hop.
Cover 20-30 meters per leg, repeat 2-3 times each side.

name: Side Shuffles
instructions: Stand in an athletic stance with knees slightly bent.
Push off the trailing foot and slide laterally.
Keep your hips low and feet shoulder-width apart.
Do not cross your feet; maintain a shuffling motion.
Cover 30-50 meters each direction, repeat 2-3 times.

name: Backwards Run
instructions: Find a clear, flat surface free of obstacles.
Begin jogging backwards at a slow pace.
Stay on the balls of your feet and reach back with each stride.
Keep your torso upright and glance over your shoulder periodically.
Cover 30-50 meters per set, repeat 2-3 times.

name: Straight-Leg Run
instructions: Run forward keeping your legs nearly straight.
Drive each leg down and back using the hip, not the knee.
Land on the ball of your foot with a quick pawing motion.
Keep your core engaged and arms pumping naturally.
Cover 30-40 meters per set, repeat 2-3 times.

name: Single-Leg Deadlift
instructions: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Hinge at the hips, lowering your torso while extending the free leg behind you.
Keep your back flat and hips square to the ground.
Lower until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor.
Return to standing by driving through the glute. Perform 10-12 reps per side.

name: Calf Raises
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart on flat ground or the edge of a step.
Rise up onto the balls of your feet as high as possible.
Hold the top position for 1-2 seconds.
Lower slowly back down, going below parallel if on a step.
Perform 15-20 repetitions for 2-3 sets.

name: Hip Hike
instructions: Stand on the edge of a step or sturdy platform on one foot.
Let the free leg hang off the side of the step.
Drop the free hip down a few inches, then raise it back up above level.
Keep the standing leg straight; the motion comes from the hip.
Perform 12-15 reps per side for 2-3 sets.

name: Monster Walk
instructions: Place a resistance band around your ankles or just above your knees.
Stand in a quarter-squat position with feet shoulder-width apart.
Step forward and diagonally outward with one foot.
Follow with the other foot, maintaining tension on the band.
Take 10-15 steps forward, then reverse. Repeat for 2-3 sets.

name: Lateral Band Walk
instructions: Place a resistance band around your ankles or just above your knees.
Stand in a quarter-squat position with feet hip-width apart.
Step laterally with one foot, then follow with the other, maintaining band tension.
Keep your hips low and back straight throughout.
Take 15-20 steps in each direction for 2-3 sets.

name: Donkey Kicks
instructions: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keep your knee bent at 90 degrees and lift one leg toward the ceiling.
Squeeze your glute at the top of the movement.
Lower the knee back down without touching the floor.
Perform 15-20 reps per side for 2-3 sets.

name: Fire Hydrant
instructions: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, lift one leg out to the side.
Raise the leg until the thigh is roughly parallel to the floor.
Hold briefly, then lower with control.
Perform 15-20 reps per side for 2-3 sets.

name: Glute Bridge March
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Drive your hips up into a bridge position, squeezing your glutes.
While holding the bridge, lift one knee toward your chest.
Lower that foot and lift the opposite knee in a marching pattern.
Perform 10-12 marches per leg for 2-3 sets, keeping hips level.

name: Standing Hip Flexor Raise
instructions: Stand tall on one leg, holding a wall for balance if needed.
Raise the opposite knee as high as possible toward your chest.
Hold for 1-2 seconds at the top.
Lower with control back to the starting position.
Perform 12-15 reps per leg for 2-3 sets.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
instructions: Stand on one foot on a step edge, letting the heel hang off.
Hold a wall or railing for balance.
Rise up on the ball of your foot as high as possible.
Lower slowly until the heel drops below the step level.
Perform 12-15 reps per side for 2-3 sets.

name: Runner's Lunge
instructions: Step forward into a deep lunge position.
Keep your front knee over your ankle and back knee hovering above the ground.
Drive through the front heel to return to standing.
Alternate legs with each repetition.
Perform 10-12 reps per leg for 2-3 sets.

name: Walking Cooldown
instructions: After finishing your run, gradually slow to a walk.
Walk at a comfortable pace for 5-10 minutes.
Focus on deep, controlled breathing to lower heart rate.
Allow your body temperature and heart rate to return to near resting.
Use this time to mentally review your workout.

name: Dynamic Stretching Routine
instructions: Begin with leg swings: 10 front-to-back and 10 side-to-side per leg.
Perform walking lunges with a torso twist for 10 reps per side.
Do inchworms for 6-8 reps to warm up the posterior chain.
Add arm circles and torso rotations for 10 reps each direction.
Finish with 10 bodyweight squats to activate the legs.

name: Foam Roll IT Band
instructions: Lie on your side with a foam roller under the outer thigh.
Support yourself with your hands and opposite foot on the floor.
Slowly roll from just below the hip to just above the knee.
Pause on any tender spots for 20-30 seconds.
Roll for 1-2 minutes per side.

name: Hip Opener Flow
instructions: Start in a deep lunge with hands on the floor inside the front foot.
Rotate the torso toward the front knee, extending the arm to the ceiling.
Return to center and straighten the front leg for a hamstring stretch.
Flow back into the lunge and repeat the rotation.
Perform 5-6 reps per side, holding each position for 3-5 seconds.

name: Leg Swing Warmup
instructions: Stand next to a wall or fence for balance support.
Swing one leg forward and backward in a controlled pendulum motion.
Gradually increase the range of motion with each swing.
Perform 15-20 swings per leg, then switch to lateral swings.
For lateral swings, face the wall and swing the leg side to side for 15-20 reps.

name: Post-Run Static Stretch
instructions: Hold each stretch for 30-45 seconds without bouncing.
Start with a standing quad stretch, pulling the heel to the glute.
Move to a standing hamstring stretch by placing the heel forward and hinging at the hips.
Perform a calf stretch against a wall, one leg at a time.
Finish with a seated figure-four stretch to open the hips and glutes.

name: Walk-Jog Warmup
instructions: Start with 3-5 minutes of brisk walking.
Transition to a very light jog for 2-3 minutes.
Alternate between walking and easy jogging for a total of 10 minutes.
Gradually increase jogging pace until you reach your desired training pace.
This warmup prepares the muscles, joints, and cardiovascular system for harder effort.

name: Jump Rope Warmup
instructions: Hold the jump rope handles at hip height with elbows close to your body.
Begin with basic two-foot jumps, clearing the rope by 1-2 inches.
Stay on the balls of your feet with soft, springy landings.
Maintain a steady rhythm for 3-5 minutes.
Progress to alternating foot jumps to mimic running cadence.
